newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end higher despite bearish USDA data.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end higher despite bearish USDA data.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures recouped early losses and settled firmer in a technically driven correction, trading sources said.
PaineWebber analyst Bernard Savaiko said the market registered oversold readings of 12 percent and 11 percent on Market Vane and Bullish Consensus, two closely watched surveys of analysts' opinions.
"Generally, readings of 25 percent or lower indicate an oversold condition, which is often followed by sharp contrarian rallies," Savaiko said in a weekly report.
May closed up 1.55 cents at 75.55 cents a lb after trading from 75.75 to 73.50 cents. The back months closed up 1.35 to 1.00.
Volume was estimated at 3,700 lots compared with Thursday's official 1,953 lots.
Support in May remained at 72.50 cents and resistance at 76.00, the high in May reached earlier this week.
Despite today's gains, there is little fundamental justification for higher prices, analysts said.

In its monthly Florida crop estimates, the U.S. Department of Agriculture raised output to 221.2 million 90-lb boxes from the record 220 million boxes forecast last month, and raised yields to 1.57 gallons per box from 1.54 gallons.
Brazil's production, meanwhile, continues to creep higher while U.S. demand remains flat, stymied by higher prices at the checkout counter.
USDA will release its next report May 12.
